title: introduce hierarchical tiled flashbridge with rotary microfusion and KV priority eviction
author: Rhea Patel
description:
Context: We've observed inconsistent tail latency and suboptimal throughput for medium-length workloads (512-4096 tokens) when using the current FlashBridge tiled path combined with rotary/rope encoded models. This PR introduces a hierarchical tiled FlashBridge implementation with a lightweight rotary microfusion path plus a KV cache priority eviction policy to improve throughput, reduce memory churn, and stabilize p95/p99 latency under continuous batching.

Motivation: Production traffic analysis (see ENG-2431) showed that: 1) the monolithic tile scheduler was frequently creating imbalanced worklets causing warp underutilization, 2) rotary position application cost was duplicated across fused kernels/host-side code paths, and 3) KV cache eviction was agnostic to prefix reuse patterns which increased cache misses during conversational workloads.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Implements a hierarchical tiler: two-level tiling that first groups heads/rows by affinity then schedules micro-tiles to streaming CUDA kernels to increase occupancy and reduce warp divergence.
- Adds a rotary microfusion path: a thin fused kernel that applies rotary embeddings inline with q/k transform in the critical fastpath to avoid an extra transpose/scale roundtrip. The kernel is corner-case safe (falls back to existing path for unsupported dtype/seq_len).
- Introduces KV priority eviction: a hot-key heuristic that tags prefixes with recent reuse and evicts cold entries first; includes a compact LRU-ish ring for fast decisions under lock-free access.
- Continuous batching scheduler tweaks: adds a small bounded queue for microtiles to favor completing existing batches rather than starting new ones (reduces partial-batch penalties).
- Feature flags and graceful rollout: runtime flags (env + Console toggle) to enable hierarchical tiler, rotary microfusion, and KV-priority eviction independently. Canary rollout steps are documented.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Hierarchical tiler improves warp utilization but introduces slight bookkeeping overhead; we measured this overhead to be outweighed for typical conversational distributions (>64 tokens avg).
- Rotary microfusion limits: it only runs for fp16/amp-safe paths on GPUs with sm >= 80; for other configurations we fall back to the existing fused-attention pipeline to preserve correctness.
- KV priority eviction is heuristic-driven; we expose tuning knobs (decay window, tag weight) in the Console to adapt for different app access patterns.

Commits (summary):
- initial hierarchical-tiler prototype and tests
- add rotary-microfusion kernel and device tests
- implement lock-free kv-priority eviction ring and metrics
- scheduler: continuous-batching microqueue and backpressure fixes
- runtime flags, console controls, and rollout script
- perf regression tests and benchmark harness updates

Changed areas (high level):
- runtime/tiler/hier_tiler.cpp (new)
- runtime/tiler/include/hier_tiler.h (new)
- runtime/kernels/rotary_microfusion.cu (new) and corresponding device_tests
- runtime/kv/priority_eviction.{cc,h} (new)
- runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp (modifications)
- sdk/telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml (added kv.evictions.tagged metric)
- docs/perf/flashbridge_hier_tiler.md (design + rollout)

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests for tiler microtile generation and boundary conditions.
- Device tests that compare rotary microfusion outputs against reference fused path across seq_len [32..8192], heads [8..32], and batch sizes [1..16].
- Integration tests for KV eviction under synthetic conversation workloads.
- Performance bench harness updated to produce steady-state measurements; CI runs synthetic perf but we also run extended benchmarks on perf-lab.

Benchmark summary (perf-lab, A100-80GB, fp16, default config):
- Throughput (tokens/sec) improvements: +28% at batch_size=4 seq_len=1024, +32% at batch_size=8 seq_len=2048, +12% for short seq_len=128 (overhead amortized).
- Latency: p50 unchanged, p95 -18%, p99 -12% under steady-state continuous batching for mixed conversation traces.
- Memory: KV cache resident memory reduced by ~22% due to priority eviction for conversational workloads with high prefix reuse.
- Regression: No measurable accuracy/regression in numerical comparisons beyond floating point tolerance.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: internal perf-canary run on dedicated perf-lab cluster (2 days).
- Stage 2: enable feature flags for 1% of traffic on hosted, monitor token throughput and error rates for 48h.
- Stage 3: increase to 10% with console toggles and monitor.
- Stage 4: full rollout with metrics-driven rollback if error rate increases >0.5% or latency regressions exceed thresholds in the playbook.

Related work: references to prior attention kernel efforts: this complements the existing FlashBridge work and is designed to be orthogonal to kernel micro-optimizations in other PRs; a follow-up may explore merging hierarchical tiler heuristics with the async KV spill conductor for even larger sequences.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit + device tests
- [x] Perf harness updates and perf-lab runs
- [x] Console flags + runtime toggles
- [x] Documentation and rollout notes

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to tiler boundary behavior with odd head counts and fallback correctness for rotary kernel. I added long comments in hier_tiler.cpp that explain the scheduling invariants.
